notes: Uber and Careem are safe and cheap. Taxis don't use meters, so agree the fare beforehand. Metro Line 1 goes to Coptic Cairo (Mar Girgis). Traffic to Giza takes 1 hour.
October to April is ideal (20-28°C). December and January mornings are 10°C and evenings are cool. During Ramadan, restaurants are closed in the daytime.
Monument entry is by card only in 2026, no cash. Book GEM timed tickets online; entering the Great Pyramid at Giza costs 1,500 EGP.
Koshary costs 50-80 EGP, ful and ta'meya 30, restaurants 300-600. Tip (baksheesh) 20-50 EGP everywhere, 10% in restaurants.
There are no 'free' photo or camel offers at the pyramids: say 'la shukran' (no thank you) and keep walking. Women will be more comfortable with shoulders and knees covered.
Take your shoes off and wear a headscarf in mosques; don't visit during Friday midday prayer.

stops.name: Giza Pyramids
stops.tips: Khufu, Khafre, Menkaure; cool and empty at the 07:00 opening. Entering the Great Pyramid costs an extra 1,500 EGP (narrow tunnel). Haggle camel rides at 200-300 EGP; pay by card.

stops.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
stops.tips: Included in the pyramid ticket. Approach from the Valley Temple; morning light hits the face.

stops.name: Panorama Point Giza
stops.tips: A desert viewpoint that takes in all three pyramids at once: the classic photo.

stops.name: Khufu's Restaurant Giza
stops.tips: Modern Egyptian cooking with pyramid views. Book ahead; 9 Pyramids Lounge is the alternative.

stops.name: Giza Sound and Light Show
stops.tips: A light and sound show in front of the Sphinx. Nights are cool; buy tickets in advance.

backups.name: 9 Pyramids Lounge
backups.tips: Lunch in the desert with pyramid views; go here if Khufu's is full.

backups.name: Giza Camel Tour
backups.tips: 30 minutes by camel in the desert; fix the price beforehand.

stops.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
stops.tips: The huge museum that opened in 2025: Tutankhamun's complete treasure (5,000 pieces) and Khufu's solar boat. Book a timed ticket online (~1,450 EGP); allow 3-4 hours and take a morning slot.

stops.name: GEM Food Court
stops.tips: Eating area inside the museum, with pyramid views.

stops.name: Grand Egyptian Museum Garden and Obelisk
stops.tips: The hanging obelisk and the outer courtyard; photograph them against the pyramid skyline.

stops.name: Koshary Abou Tarek
stops.tips: Cairo's most famous koshary (rice, lentils and pasta) since the 1950s. Downtown, four floors, 80 EGP.

backups.name: Zooba Downtown
backups.tips: Modern Egyptian street food: ta'meya and hawawshi.

backups.name: Egyptian Museum Tahrir
backups.tips: The old museum, with the mummies and artefacts that were not moved to the GEM.

stops.name: Citadel of Saladin & Muhammad Ali Mosque
stops.tips: The citadel and the alabaster mosque; the terrace has views over Cairo and the pyramids.

stops.name: Sultan Hassan Mosque
stops.tips: A Mamluk masterpiece, with a huge courtyard and a sense of calm.

stops.name: Al-Muizz Street
stops.tips: A Fatimid street of mosques, sabils (public fountains) and the Beit el-Suhaymi house, lit up at night.

stops.name: Naguib Mahfouz Cafe
stops.tips: Run by Oberoi inside Khan el-Khalili. Try the molokhia (jute leaf stew) and mint tea; air-conditioned.

stops.name: Khan el-Khalili
stops.tips: A 14th-century bazaar selling copper, spices and papyrus. Bargain down to a third of the first price; El Fishawy cafe is open 24 hours.

backups.name: El Fishawy Cafe
backups.tips: A mirrored cafe since 1773; mint tea and shisha.

backups.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
backups.tips: A mosque-university since 970; visit instead of Sultan Hassan.

stops.name: Hanging Church
stops.tips: A 3rd-century church built over a Roman fortress, in Coptic Cairo. Take the metro to Mar Girgis.

stops.name: Coptic Museum
stops.tips: Coptic art and the Nag Hammadi texts.

stops.name: Ben Ezra Synagogue
stops.tips: Said to be where Moses was found; home of the Cairo Geniza.

stops.name: Abou El Sid Zamalek
stops.tips: Egyptian cooking in 1920s decor in Zamalek: stuffed pigeon and molokhia.

stops.name: Nile Felucca Ride
stops.tips: One hour on a sailing felucca from Zamalek. Go at sunset and haggle per boat.

backups.name: Sequoia Zamalek
backups.tips: A riverside terrace on the Nile; shisha and meze, instead of the felucca.

backups.name: Cairo Tower
backups.tips: A 187 m tower in Zamalek with city views.

stops.name: Saqqara Step Pyramid
stops.tips: The world's oldest pyramid (Djoser). The Serapeum's underground bull sarcophagi need an extra ticket; cooler in the morning.

stops.name: Dahshur Red Pyramid
stops.tips: Entry into the Red Pyramid is included (steep tunnel). Next to the Bent Pyramid, with few tourists.

stops.name: Memphis Open Air Museum
stops.tips: The ancient capital, with a colossal statue of Ramses II and an alabaster sphinx.

stops.name: Saqqara Country Club Lunch
stops.tips: A farm restaurant among palm trees: grills and Egyptian bread.

stops.name: Saqqara Carpet School
stops.tips: A hand-woven carpet workshop; no pressure to buy, just watch.

backups.name: Abou Shakra Giza
backups.tips: A kebab classic; stop on the way back.

backups.name: Bent Pyramid Dahshur
backups.tips: Inside the Bent Pyramid; go instead of the Red Pyramid.

stops.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
stops.tips: 2.5 hours by train from Cairo; a modern library and museums in a disc-shaped building.

stops.name: Qaitbay Citadel
stops.tips: A 15th-century fortress on the site of the ancient lighthouse, with Mediterranean views.

stops.name: Fish Market Restaurant Alexandria
stops.tips: Fish on the Corniche: pick yours from the counter, with Mediterranean views.

stops.name: Kom El Shoqafa Catacombs
stops.tips: Roman-era underground tombs, mixing Egyptian and Greek styles.

stops.name: Alexandria Corniche
stops.tips: Walk the seafront boulevard and take the tram to Montaza; the return train is at 18:00.

backups.name: Mohamed Ahmed Foul Alexandria
backups.tips: Alexandria's classic for ful and falafel.

backups.name: Pompey's Pillar
backups.tips: A Roman column; go instead of the catacombs.

stops.name: Gezira Island Zamalek Walk
stops.tips: The island district: ivy-covered embassy streets and the Nile.

stops.name: Aisha Fahmy Palace
stops.tips: An Art Nouveau palace and gallery in Zamalek.

stops.name: Ovio Zamalek
stops.tips: Zamalek's breakfast and brunch cafe; a farewell meal.

stops.name: Zamalek Nile Bank Last Tea
stops.tips: A last tea at a cafe with Nile views; the airport is 45 minutes away.

backups.name: Cairo Kitchen Zamalek
backups.tips: Home cooking; go instead of Ovio.

backups.name: Museum of Islamic Art Cairo
backups.tips: One of the world's best collections of Islamic art; go instead of the Zamalek plan.
